Not refuted, but the cliff's LOCATION is a reading artifact and the real exposure is wider: my probe (tools/alignment_skeptic_blend_pa.py, same file blend_probe) evaluates the same two angles on the BLENDED onset groove the model builds: the cap-side angle is 89.19 at K 0.003 and stays above the claim-mu gate 38.03 up to K 8.11 (above 35.03 to K 8.58), while the 35.25 the gate reads sits at the linear law's K 0 corner the built groove does not have; the pin-side (forward-drive) angle peaks 30.94, under 43 - atan(mu) to mu 0.214 (0.25 on the judge's 45 rule). So either the cap-side gate does not govern at a dwell exit (then the mu 0.136 cliff is an artifact and the forward drive holds to ~0.21) or the built groove fails its own gate at the claim's mu 0.087 as well. Either way no one has shown the dwell exit transmits under friction; the watch stands until a force analysis with friction (both load paths) through the blend is on file. See missed[0].
